title: Gallery caption approval
brief:
You coordinate a gallery exhibition featuring work by local printmakers. Write an email to one participating artist about their wall caption. Their submission form lists the piece as Between Stops, a two-color linocut made in 2024. The label spreadsheet instead lists Between Stations and 2025. Ask the artist to confirm the title, year, and medium by Tuesday at 3 p.m., when labels go to print. Mention that their exhibition listing can still be updated afterward if they need more time.

Aim for 70 to 150 words. Return the complete original work directly in your answer. Do not sign or identify yourself. Do not use tools.

8d5e74fc28e44b63.text:
Subject: Please confirm your wall caption by Tuesday at 3 p.m.

Hi,

I’m checking the wall caption for your print before the labels go to print. Your submission form lists the work as *Between Stops*, a two-color linocut made in 2024. The label spreadsheet lists the title as *Between Stations* and the year as 2025.

Could you reply with the title, year, and medium exactly as you’d like them to appear? The labels go to print on Tuesday at 3 p.m., so please send your confirmation by then. If you need more time, we can still update your exhibition listing afterward.

Thanks for checking these details.

6f00fd87c133cbd5.text:
**Subject: Please confirm your exhibition wall caption**

Hi,

Could you confirm the title, year, and medium for your piece by Tuesday at 3 p.m.? That’s when the wall labels go to print.

Your submission form lists *Between Stops*, a two-color linocut made in 2024. Our label spreadsheet lists *Between Stations* and 2025. Please let me know which title and year we should use and whether “two-color linocut” is the correct medium.

If you need more time to check, we can still update your exhibition listing after Tuesday’s print deadline.
